title: fathom status --json
description: Who is keeping this repository's index current, what it costs, and what is left to do: the headless answer behind `fathom daemon`'s health, ADR-004 §7.1's client fallback chain, and the same index and cache sections `fathom stats` prints. Owner: `e6.3`.

daemon.description: The `daemon` section: what a live daemon said about itself over the socket, or what the client reconstructed from the lease file and the watcher's heartbeat when nothing answered. The two halves are separated by `source`, which is the whole point of the field: a live process, a dead process's lock, a dead watcher's last note and nothing at all are four different facts. A running daemon's own keys are governed by the socket protocol id it reports in `protocol` (`fathom.daemon/1`), not by this schema — they are listed here because the human printer reads them, and they are `additionalProperties: true` so a daemon can grow without breaking a client.

source.description: Where this section came from. `daemon` means a live process answered; anything else means the client read a file a process left, and says which.

running.description: `true` exactly when `source` is `daemon`. A script that wants to know whether anything is watching reads this and not a zero.

protocol.description: The socket protocol the answering daemon speaks.

shutdown.description: Set only while the daemon is leaving: the reason it is finishing, so a client that raced the exit can tell a stop from a crash.

lease.description: The writer lease: its path, whether a live process holds it, the holder's record when there is one, and `broken` when a dead holder's claim was taken over (ADR-004 §7.1).

socket.description: The IPC endpoint: kind, path, whether anything is listening, and `reason` when there is no endpoint on this platform or path.

cpu.description: The budgeted background indexing: configured share, measured share, the window it was measured over, how many windows went over, how long the loop slept to pay for them, and whether a foreground client was recently heard.

source.description: `proc` is user+system CPU the kernel charged the process; `estimate` is busy wall time, which is an upper bound and is labelled as one.

queue.description: The request queue and the counters that make "three TUIs and a CLI made one pass" an assertion: pushed, coalesced, shed, served, depth, bound, high water.

hooks.description: The ADR-005 event stream as the daemon reads it: the durable offset, bytes still unread (the lag the cap produces rather than drops), and the back-pressure state.

passes.description: Indexing passes: how many, how many clients they settled, and the requests grouped by origin — the counters the ticket's first criterion is asserted with.

watch.description: The watcher's own state machine: phase, backend, debounce, what it is waiting for.

heartbeat.description: Only when nothing answered: the last status file a `fathom watch` or daemon wrote, with the age read off the file's own mtime. A dead process's note, labelled as one.

pass.description: Only with `--index`: the daemon's answer to the pass this verb asked for — whether it settled, and what the pass read.

x-fathom-exit-codes.name: OK
x-fathom-exit-codes.when: the verb answered; a daemon running or absent is both OK, and `daemon.running` says which

x-fathom-exit-codes.name: ERROR
x-fathom-exit-codes.when: a rejected argument value, or a report that could not be rendered

x-fathom-exit-codes.name: USAGE
x-fathom-exit-codes.when: clap rejected the command line (bad flag, unknown verb, missing argument)

x-fathom-exit-codes.name: FEATURE_ABSENT
x-fathom-exit-codes.when: the binary was built without the `watch` feature, which is what carries the daemon

x-fathom-exit-codes.name: INDEX_DEGRADED
x-fathom-exit-codes.when: the index is missing, stale or mid-rebuild, or the writer lease on disk belongs to a writer that is gone
